newsitem.title: UK: Britain sends reconnaissance party to Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Britain sends reconnaissance party to Zaire.

text.p: Britain on Friday sent a 43-strong reconnaissance party to central Africa to see if it can help ease the humanitarian crisis in Zaire.
Their job is to check the conditions on the ground for any contribution that Britain might make to a multinational force.

The reconnaissance party, headed by rapid deployment force chief Brigadier John Thompson, flew initially to the Kenyan capital of Nairobi and Entebbe in Uganda to assess the use of their airports as staging posts to Zaire.
The party will then travel to Goma and Bukavu in Zaire for an on-the-spot review of the situation. It will return to Britain on Monday to brief military chiefs.
Britain has cautioned it would not send a larger force until the nature of its mission to help more than a million starving refugees was absolutely clear.
Prime Minister John Major said Western governments had a strong moral obligation to help ease the crisis and Britain was ready in principle to join a Canadian-led international force.
But he told parliament on Thursday that the situation on the ground was complex, the terrain was very tough and there was no clear ceasefire between Tutsi rebels and their Hutu foes.
